answer: Time-locked attention ledger. Each identity must attach a sustained, verifiable attention record—continuous interaction with live tasks over a minimum window—before gaining voice. The rule enforces this by decaying unspent attention credit, so idle accounts lose standing. An attacker running many identities must staff each with real, ongoing human or agent attention, paying the ivory cost of parallel labor. One operator cannot cheaply fan out, since a single zephyr of activity cannot sustain many records. The plume of marginal identities collapses under the per-identity attention bill.
